newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jingwei sees improving earnings.
newsitem.headline: Jingwei sees improving earnings.

text.p: China's Jingwei Textile Machinery Co said on Tuesday it expected improvement in group earnings in the second half of this year and next year.
"Our earnings will be better in the second half than in the first half, and better in 1997 than in 1996," vice-chairman and general manager Liu Shitong told a news conference.
The company earlier announced interim net profit of 35.72 million yuan in the first half of this year. Turnover stood at 330.37 million yuan in the first half.
It expected more favourable business environement in the second half because of the expected relaxation of China's austerity measures and rising living standard, Liu said.
Chairman Mei Zaisen added demand for textile machines was expected to increase because China's Ninth Five-year plan called for more technological reforms.
The country's rate cuts last week would benefit China's textile industry, which would in turn have a positive impact on the company, Liu noted.
Jingwei expected to be able to achieve its 1996 sales target of 750 million yuan this year, Liu said.
But he expected exports, which declined in the first half, would not improve much in the second half.
Exports fell to 23.68 million yuan in the first half of 1996 from 45.36 million yuan in the year-ago period.
Liu attributed the decline to political problems in a few export markets, such as Bangladesh.
